title: Zugzwang Windmill: Leave One Pawn Move
summary: Keep the black king confined while allowing a forced pawn capture that prevents stalemate and releases your passer.

nodes.question: Black has just played ...h6. Why is a king move better than either pawn move?
nodes.explanation: The black king is trapped on a1. Kc2 keeps b1 and b2 covered while leaving ...hxg5 available. Moving g5 or capturing h6 instead would leave Black with no legal move: stalemate.

branches.title: Source finish with an explicit legal bridge
commentary: Begin after the forced ...h6 between the 54- and 56-second samples. The before-and-after boards establish the bridge ...h6/Kc2/hxg5; the earlier eight-piece waiting sequence is outside this proof.
Kc2 preserves the king cage: b1 and b2 are covered. It is the only winning move; the move leaves Black a pawn capture instead of stalemating it.
hxg5 is Black’s only legal reply. The pawn from h6 captures White’s g5 pawn, while Black’s other h-pawn remains on h5.
hxg5 recaptures with the pawn from h4. White now has a passed g-pawn and has freed h4 for Black’s remaining h-pawn.
h4 is Black’s only legal move. White has preserved a pawn move so the confined king is not stalemated.
g6 advances the passer while White’s king keeps the corner sealed.
h3 gives Black another legal pawn move. It approaches promotion, but it will not rescue the king cage.
g7 prepares White’s promotion first. The black king still cannot move.
h2 brings Black’s pawn one step from queening. White can promote now without giving stalemate, because Black retains its h-pawn move.
g8=Q creates White’s queen. Black can still promote, so the game continues.
h1=Q is the source’s chosen promotion. Black’s only legal moves are promotions on h1, including underpromotions. The new queen does not give check to Kc2.
Qg7# mates on the long diagonal to a1. Black’s a2 pawn occupies a2 and Kc2 covers b1/b2. Black’s queen on h1 cannot block the g7–a1 diagonal.
branches.explanation: Qg7# mates on the long diagonal to a1. Black’s a2 pawn occupies a2 and Kc2 covers b1/b2. Black’s queen on h1 cannot block the g7–a1 diagonal.

exercises.prompt: Why deliberately let Black capture g5?
exercises.answer: After Kc2, ...hxg5 is Black’s only legal move. White recaptures from h4, which opens h4 for the remaining black pawn and avoids stalemate.

exercises.prompt: Why does Black getting a queen fail to save the game?
exercises.answer: White queens first and Black’s h1=Q gives no check. Qg7 then mates along the long diagonal while Kc2 keeps the corner exits covered.
